summary:
L.E.W.I.S. is an interactive lunar exploration and landing planning website that helps users understand how location, timing, and mission priorities affect conditions on the Moon.

Historical Exploration lets users select Apollo landing missions and simulate their original coordinates at a different launch time. The simulation estimates arrival using the mission’s original travel duration, evaluates sunlight and Earth visibility, and checks whether selected environmental criteria are satisfied. Results show the remaining delay allowance, the latest valid launch and landing times, and a recommended alternative site when available.

Future Exploration starts with mission objectives, including landing demonstrations, resource prospecting, solar operations, communications, or custom goals. Users adjust sliders for slope, elevation, Earth visibility, water-related indicators, illumination, and surface hazards. Changing the landing date or hour compares the original recommendation with an updated site.

An interactive 3D Moon supports rotation, zooming, coordinate selection, and clickable markers that open ground views. Surface controls display terrain, lighting, resources, hazards, and Earth visibility.
